results.why: Starts below the floor. Recovery must climb, not freeze. Was a KNOWN FAILURE from 2026-10-07 to 2026-10-09: a FALSE fail-safe through edge X6. The recovery climbs from 3 m and converges (AltitudeFix sizes the climb to reach the band in one lookahead, so it slows near the floor), but the position had then been illegal for T = 5 s with the Shield still intervening, and X6, which tested duration only, sent the aircraft to RTL at 9.45 m, 0.55 m short of the floor. The grant's fail-safe is for a repair that is unsafe ("trigger fail-safe (RTL / Land) when repair is unsafe", Safety Shield p1), and this one was working. Since 2026-10-09 X6 leaves a recovery alone while its illegal depth is shown to fall (guardrail/fsm.py, x6_min_escape_mps): the flight takes G1 then G7, reaches the band at 6.3 s and completes. Re-measured 2026-10-11 on both theta readings and with the onset limit at 1 s and 0 s; the marker was removed then. With the FSM off the flight is the LEGACY one (tests/test_sweep.py). At the grant's 5 s forecast (2026-10-12) it reaches the band at 10.3 s (G1 at 0 s, G7 at 12.3 s): AltitudeFix sizes the climb to arrive in one LOOKAHEAD, so a longer lookahead climbs more gently (see altitude-recovery-depth for the arithmetic). Still one recovery, no fail-safe, and the purpose holds. Since 2026-10-29 the recovery climbs at the policy's 2 m/s cap (the Shield's recovery_law "cap", WP3-17): 7 m to the floor in 3.6 s, 36 repairs (103 before).

results.why: The grant's worked example, flown: "Polygon NFZ spawns 60 m ahead at t=15s, translates 5 m/s perpendicular to flight path" - here a 40 x 20 m zone spawned 30 m ahead at 5 s and translating `zone_mps` to the aircraft's left (translate_polygon_fence with mps / direction: a constant dynamic_nfz motion), so it slides across the route and off it again. The Shield forecasts the zone's motion over its lookahead: the aircraft must never enter it and never be unsafe. The zone moves sideways only, so it never sweeps over a waiting aircraft. Its instruction (the grant example's task prompt, in this family's words) is flown in two paraphrased wordings beside the canonical one (`paraphrase`); the headless pilot reads no text, so the arms are a plumbing check, never a robustness number.

results.why: A time_window_switch hot-applied mid-flight with its own weekly window: at 1 s the harness sends "release nfz-school, weekdays 12:00-12:30" (deactivate_rule with a window) while the aircraft is held at the zone's edge on a Monday at 11:59:50. The switch comes into force at 12:00:00, 10 s in; the Shield must keep the fence bound until then and release it after, on the conservative side of the edge, and the mission must then complete. Phase 0 is before the event, phase 1 between the event and the switch, phase 2 after it.

results.why: A zone whose breach action is RTL is hot-applied `ahead_m` in front of the aircraft at 3 s. The Shield does not project around it: the rule asks for RTL, so it stops where a stop is legal and the escalation FSM goes straight to RTL (edge G11). The autopilot's RTL flies home, behind the aircraft, away from the zone. Labelled RTL_triggered with a fail-safe expected; the aircraft must never enter the zone.
